sourcedFrom: SilencerCo Scythe-Ti 30 Field Manual — 2023 edition (the file the maker published as scythe-manual_2023.pdf) (2023)
cleanIntro: ⛔ The Scythe-Ti is a sealed can. SilencerCo publishes no way to take it apart, and the maintenance it does publish is short: keep the mount clean, keep the threads clean, and if the bore needs anything at all it gets a BRUSH — never a patch. The whole job is about the mounting interface, because that is the part that can fail dangerously.

steps.title: Firearm unloaded and the action OPEN before the can moves
steps.action: Open the action and see that the firearm is visibly clear of ammunition — before the silencer goes on and before it comes off. A suppressed gun is quieter, not safer, and the book says so in as many words.
steps.quote: Before installing the silencer on the host firearm, be sure the firearm is unloaded and the action is opened so the firearm is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Scythe-Ti 30 Field Manual — 2023 edition (the file the maker published as scythe-manual_2023.pdf) — WARNING

steps.title: ⛔ Re-check tightness every 30 rounds
steps.action: Silencers back off under recoil, and a partly-unthreaded can is how baffle strikes happen. SilencerCo names an interval rather than leaving it to feel: verify the attachment is secure after about 30 discharges.
steps.quote: To ensure your silencer remains secure while firing, it is of the utmost importance that you frequently verify the silencer is securely tightened onto the barrel. We recommend checking the security of the attachment after 30 discharges of the firearm.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Scythe-Ti 30 Field Manual — 2023 edition (the file the maker published as scythe-manual_2023.pdf) — WARNING

steps.title: Mounts get the solvent and the brush
steps.action: The mount is where carbon and fouling collect and where a loose fit turns into a baffle strike. Standard gun cleaning solvent and a brush, periodically — that is the maintenance this can actually needs.
steps.quote: The Scythe-Ti 30 typically requires limited maintenance. Mounts should periodically be cleaned with any standard gun cleaning solvent and a brush to remove any carbon or fouling.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Scythe-Ti 30 Field Manual — 2023 edition (the file the maker published as scythe-manual_2023.pdf) — Maintenance

steps.title: ⛔ Bore: a brush if it needs one, NEVER a patch
steps.action: If the bore has light fouling, run a cleaning BRUSH through it. Do not run patches: a patch can come off inside the silencer, sit there invisibly, and cause damage the next time the gun is fired. This is the single most important don't in the whole book.
steps.quote: Do not run cleaning patches through the bore as the patches might become lodged in the silencer and cause damage upon firing.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Scythe-Ti 30 Field Manual — 2023 edition (the file the maker published as scythe-manual_2023.pdf) — Maintenance

steps.title: ⛔ No chlorine, no acetone — and expect colour change
steps.action: The Scythe-Ti's titanium finish has its own rules. SilencerCo recommends a rust-preventive firearm lubricant and a microfibre towel, warns that any such lubricant may change the colour of the can, and bans chlorine and acetone products outright.
steps.aside: Any rust-preventing firearm lubricants will work, but they may change the color of the Scythe-Ti.
steps.quote: Do not use chlorine or acetone products on Scythe-Ti.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Scythe-Ti 30 Field Manual — 2023 edition (the file the maker published as scythe-manual_2023.pdf) — Maintenance

steps.title: ⛔ Never fire it without the Anchor Brake or a front cap
steps.action: Firing the Scythe-Ti 30 with no Anchor Brake and no SilencerCo front cap fitted negates the point of the silencer and voids the warranty. Check the front of the can is actually complete before you mount it.
steps.quote: Firing the Scythe-Ti 30 without the Anchor Brake or a SilencerCo front cap will negate benefits of using a silencer and will void the warranty.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Scythe-Ti 30 Field Manual — 2023 edition (the file the maker published as scythe-manual_2023.pdf) — Assembly

deepAbsentReason: SilencerCo publishes NO disassembly for the Scythe-Ti. Its maintenance section is one paragraph — "The Scythe-Ti 30 typically requires limited maintenance. Mounts should periodically be cleaned with any standard gun cleaning solvent and a brush to remove any carbon or fouling." — plus a bore brush and an explicit ban on patches. ⛔ AND A NEARBY SILENCERCO PROCEDURE DOES NOT TRANSFER TO THIS CAN. Some SilencerCo silencers — the rimfire and pistol-calibre models — do publish a full baffle-stack strip, and those instructions are easy to find. They are not instructions for the Scythe-Ti. Following them here would mean forcing apart an assembly SilencerCo never documents coming apart, and the likely results are a damaged silencer and a warranty that no longer covers it. A sealed can stays sealed: clean the mount, the threads and the outside, brush the bore, and leave the inside to SilencerCo.

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Standard gun solvent and a brush on the mount, periodically
Carbon and fouling off the threads and shouldering surface
⛔ Check for a gap at the shoulder before every session

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: A cleaning BRUSH only, for light fouling
⛔ NEVER a patch — it can lodge inside and cause damage on firing

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped down; carbon off the outside of the tube
⛔ Solvents used with ventilation, skin and eye protection

cleaning.name: ⛔ WHAT YOU DO NOT DO
tasks: This can does not come apart — no disassembly is published for an owner
Anything wrong with it goes back to SilencerCo under the lifetime warranty

reassembly: Threads and shouldering surface clean and dry before it goes back on.
Silencer threaded on by hand, taking care not to cross-thread, until firmly secured.
⛔ No visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the mount.
fncheck: Back on the host: thread it on until it is firmly secured with no barrel thread still visible, then check the shoulder for a gap by eye and by fingernail. ⛔ If there is any gap, do not fire it. Re-check tightness after about 30 rounds, and look through the bore for obstructions before the first shot of any session.
